title: Refactor shared Terraform modules and upgrade cloud provider plugins
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Our Terraform repository contains duplicated networking and compute resource definitions across services. Multiple teams maintain slightly different copies of the same VPC/subnet/route table and IAM module code. We're running an older AWS provider (v4.x) and several modules pin to deprecated patterns that block newer provider features (for example: aws_lb_listener default_action deprecations and aws_security_group inline rules limitations).

Goal: Consolidate and refactor the shared Terraform modules into a single, well-documented set of reusable modules (vpc, subnet, nat-gateway, security-groups, iam-roles, autoscaling). Upgrade cloud provider plugins (AWS provider to v6.x or compatible minor) and Terraform CLI constraints to 1.5+ where required. Deliver a migration plan that minimizes risk to production and preserves state history.

Scope:
- Create canonical module interfaces for networking and compute used by hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Remove duplicated templates and update callers across 12 service repos.
- Upgrade aws and random providers and update provider configurations for multi-region usage.
- Migrate state for renamed/relocated modules with state migration scripts and documented refresh steps.
- Add CI checks (tflint, tfsec scan updates) and pre-apply sanity tests in staging.

Out-of-scope: Rewriting critical runtime IaC (k8s operator manifests) or full cloud migration. Those are separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Shared modules (vpc, subnet, security-groups, iam, autoscaling) exist in registry path modules/shared-v1 and include README with inputs/outputs and migration notes.
All consuming repos (list provided in links) updated to reference modules/shared-v1 with no drift detected after terraform plan in staging.
AWS provider upgraded to v6.x across monorepo with provider blocks consolidated to root where possible; no production changes after controlled canary deploys.
State migrations executed using documented terraform state mv plans and validated by running full plan/apply in a non-production account.
CI pipeline includes tflint and tfsec with new rules and fails on severity >= medium; documented remediation steps included.
Runbook for rollbacks and emergency state restore created and reviewed by SRE and Infra owners.
Performance: Applying common networking module reduces plan time for a representative service by >= 20% in staging due to module reuse and fewer resources defined per repo.
tasks: Inventory: enumerate repos and current module copies (ENG-7045 output).
Design canonical module interfaces and publish API contract (inputs/outputs).
Implement shared modules in modules/shared-v1 with unit examples.
Write migration scripts and terraform state mv plans for each consumer repo.
Upgrade providers and run automated compatibility fixes (providers.tf, variable schemas).
Create CI checks and add to repo template used by infra teams.
Coordinate staged rollout: dev -> staging -> prod canary for three low-traffic services, validate, then wider rollout.
Post-merge validation: perform drift detection and run terraform-compliance test-suite in staging.

implementation_notes: Prefer explicit input variables over implicit lookups to keep module boundaries clear.
Avoid changing resource addresses in-place when possible; where unavoidable, create a small window with state mv + terraform apply in one operation.
Use semantic versioning for modules and publish to internal registry; tag v1.0.0 only after all three canaries succeed.
Add a pre-upgrade compatibility test that runs 'terraform 0.12upgrade' style checks for schema changes before TOC.
Document known incompatibilities for provider upgrade (aws provider: some load balancer attributes removed; refer to provider changelog).
